author: EmuCore - Hub
title: How shadPS4 turns game tests into useful compatibility evidence
summary: The official compatibility workflow records repeatable test results, hardware context and status changes so progress can be measured without relying on a single screenshot.
heroAlt: Gameplay screenshot distributed in the official shadPS4 repository
searchKeywords: How shadPS4 turns game tests into useful compatibility evidence

blocks.text: Five statuses describe how far a game gets

The compatibility repository uses the fixed statuses `status-nothing`, `status-boots`, `status-menus`, `status-ingame`, and `status-playable`. `Nothing` means there is no useful visual or audio output. `Boots` means the game starts and produces initial video or audio before freezing or crashing. `Menus` reaches the menus but cannot continue into gameplay. `Ingame` reaches gameplay with errors that prevent completion, while `Playable` means the game can be completed without serious issues. These are outcome definitions, not performance scores.
Reports target major releases, not nightly snapshots

The rules accept results from major shadPS4 releases such as v0.17.0 and reject nightly or work-in-progress builds for the primary record. The issue form makes that a required checkbox. A fixed release gives every report a reproducible emulator baseline; rapidly changing pre-release commits would otherwise mix several code states under one status label. Updates after a later major release belong in the existing issue comments with a new log.
The issue form records identity and test environment

Required fields include Game Name, Game serial, Game version, emulator version, Current status, Operating System, Description and Log File. The serial example uses the CUSA format, and the OS dropdown distinguishes Windows, Linux and macOS. Processor, graphics card, error text and screenshots are available for additional context. The form also tells reporters to enable synchronous logging and to attach the untouched file from `user/log`.
CUSA plus operating system controls duplication

The repository allows one report for a game and OS combination, with separate entries when the operating system differs or the regional CUSA identifier differs. If the same CUSA and OS already exist, testers should comment on the older issue with the new major-release result, description, screenshots and log rather than create a duplicate. This keeps a title’s progression visible without collapsing platform-specific behavior into one row.
Clean dumps, stock timing and sys_modules protect the baseline

Reports must use an owned, unmodified dump: patches and FPKG repackaging are excluded. Behavior-changing options such as PS4 Neo mode, Devkit Console mode and Vblank Frequency must remain untouched. Experimental readbacks or Direct Memory Access can be accepted but receive an `experimental` label. The README also lists required legally dumped firmware libraries for `sys_modules`, including audio-decoder, font, JPEG, JSON, libc, NGS2, PNG and RTC modules.
The workflow turns issue forms into compatibility_data.json

`.github/workflows/update_game_compatibility.yml` reads GitHub issues through the API, extracts form sections such as Game Name and Game serial, recognizes CUSA identifiers, then inspects `os-*` and `status-*` labels. Its generated JSON is keyed first by serial and then by operating system; each record stores issue number, name, serial, last-tested timestamp, status, milestone version and all labels. The job runs on pushes, manual dispatch and a three-hour schedule, and only publishes a release when the generated database passes its size check.
